answers.solution:
Done. I reproduced all four failure modes live and verified the fix end-to-end, including a full run of the delivered script under a `PATH` with **no `make`/`cc`/`gcc`/`ld`**.

## Deliverables

- **`/home/kara/bootstrap-make-userspace.sh`** — tested, self-contained bootstrap script (`--zig`, `--make-src`, `--prefix`, `--work`, `--static`).
- **`/home/kara/SOLUTION-gnu-make-userspace-bootstrap.md`** — the markdown solution: title, root-cause analysis, exact fix, verification.

## What was actually verified

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Wall 1: no compiler | `C compiler cannot create executables` (rc=77) |
| Wall 3: no working make + dep-tracking on | `Something went wrong bootstrapping makefile fragments` (rc=1) |
| Wall 4: inner `>/dev/null` | `make.log` = **0 bytes** |
| Native build with zig wrappers | GNU Make 4.4.1 built, `TOY_OK` |
| Static musl build | `statically linked`, 2.25 MB, `TOY_OK` |
| Delivered script, bare `PATH` (fullbin minus toolchain) | `SCRIPT_RC=0`, log = 39446 bytes |
| `bash -n` on all rendered wrappers | `cc/gcc/c++/ld OK` |
| Toy target with system `make` shadowed by rc=127 stub | `TOY_OK` |
| Input checksums | zig + make tarballs match published SHA-256 |

## The four fixes (root causes)

1. **Order + explicit tools** — bootstrap Make only after the zig C toolchain, and export `CC`/`CXX`/`LD` rather than defaulting to `cc`.
2. **Wrap the linker too** — no `ld` on bare agents and no `zig ld`; use `printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec "%s" ld.lld "$@"\n' "$ZIGB" > "$BIN/ld"`.
3. **Break the chicken-and-egg** — `--disable-nls --disable-dependency-tracking`, make `configure` exit-code-tolerant, always run the self-contained `build.sh`.
4. **Never silence the log** — one log file, no inner `/dev/null`; plus `bash -n` every heredoc/rendered remote script *after* rendering.

The script also uses `--static` (musl) for a glibc-independent binary, which is the safer default for heterogeneous bare agents.
